title: 007 First Light’s Switch 2 Edition Delayed Yet Again, Here’s How Long You Have To Wait
description: Developer IO has confirmed that 007 First Light's Switch 2 edition has been delayed for a second time. It's now scheduled for March 2027. The studio said in a notice that First Light's Switch 2 version was delayed "to ensure we deliver the quality of experience players expect." "This additional time will go toward polishing the Nintendo Switch 2 performance of the game," IO said. First Light's Switch 2 version was playable at Gamescom recently, and IO said it was "thrilled by the positive feedback." The same demo will be at Tokyo Game Show this week in Japan. "Thank you for your patience, understanding, and continued support," IO said. First Light's Switch 2 version was originally set to launch alongside the console and PC editions in May, but was later delayed to Summer 2026. Another delay for the Switch 2 edition seemed likely given that Summer officially ends on September 22 and IO had not communicated a release date. Another reason another delay for the Switch 2 edition is not that surprising is because IO boss Hakan Abrak said back in May that the game needed "a bit more time to get it where we want it to be." At the time, Abrak said the game was now targeting late-Summer, but now it's been delayed to 2027. “We just want to make sure it’s good as it can be. I don’t want to hear it wasn’t a good version," Abrak told The Game Business. First Light sold more than 4 million copies and earned rave reviews. All the signs are pointing to a sequel, but it has not been officially announced yet.

title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Brings Back Snowboarding, And Red XIII Might Steal The Show Again
description: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is aiming to end the remake trilogy with a bang, and alongside the main campaign, there'll be plenty of other activities to tackle when you're not racing to stop Sephiroth from destroying the planet. Snowboarding is one such distraction, as the iconic minigame from the original Final Fantasy 7 is back, and Square Enix is suggesting that something wild could take place in it. An activity that can be accessed at the Golden Saucer, game director Naoki Hamaguchi hasn't gone into too many details about it just yet, but he did tease that Square Enix knows that there are a lot of "high expectations" surrounding it. Especially when Red XIII (Nanaki) takes part in that event. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LRA759MHPJs "I can say that this snowboarding section will be in Revelation, and all of the party members, you'll see them, um, in that snowboarding section. But Nanaki might not be on a snowboard," Hamaguchi said to GameSpot. "You'll have to like look forward to what he's going to be riding. I think it's going to get a lot of attention." Red XIII stole the limelight in several scenes throughout Final Fantasy 7 Remake and Rebirth, thanks to moments where he attempted to blend in with the bipedal cast. From donning a disguise to take part in the Queen's Blood tournament to visiting his adopted family in Cosmo Canyon, he's been responsible for some of the biggest laughs and surprises in the series so far. A new trailer for Final Fantasy 7 Revelation dropped during the recent PlayStation State of Play broadcast, revealing more of the game and its April 2028 release date. GamneSpot also went hands-on with the Final Fantasy 7 Revelation at Gamescom last month, where we got a taste of just how massive the game is going to be with its expanded open-world design.

title: Diablo 5 Doubles Down On The Darkness, But Hope Still Has A Place In Sanctuary
description: Diablo's world of Sanctuary isn't a top tourist destination, thanks to roaming monsters and demonic forces looking to corrupt humanity, and in Diablo 5, everything has gone to hell--quite literally! Unlike the previous games in the series, which revolved around saving Sanctuary from Diablo and his Prime Evil Kin, Diablo 5 kicks off long after the Lord of Terror has conquered the land. In a world this bleak, how will players find the motivation to keep going when evil has already triumphed? Speaking to GameSpot at BlizzCon, the Diablo team discussed the grim setting of Diablo 5, as well as the glimmers of hope that still exist even during Diablo's post-apocalyptic reign. Human strongholds are no more, survivors are scattered across the land, and things look bleaker than usual for players when they set foot in that world. According to Blizzard, not only is Diablo 5 keeping the grim, dark atmosphere of Diablo 4 intact and doubling down on it, but the landscape will also reflect humanity's fall. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=blmyIDbxN2o&pp=0gcJCf4LAYcqIYzv "We need to tell a story of this apocalyptic Sanctuary, executive producer Matt Zitterman said. "Sanctuary is already a pretty dark place. How do we double down on that darkness and go even further? That's where the ideas of thinking about our world as being built in layers--a layer about the past, a layer about the present, and a layer about the future--really came to light. And with that, you know, the past is all about telling the stories of what happened to humanity when Diablo overtook Sanctuary." "A lot of games do this extremely well. There are little vignettes and stories that are told visually about how humans were trying to survive and ultimately failed, and we want those parts of the world, those parts of Sanctuary, to really tell that story." Zitterman added that Sanctuary's state in Diablo 5 is akin to a forest fire, both during and after a devastating blaze has swept through an area. "We use the metaphor of a forest fire a lot," Zitterman explained. "A forest fire ravages through a place and leaves behind a changed landscape. And we see that as kind of the parts of the world that represent the battlefields of where demons were fought, and ultimately, humans lost. But the landscape was forever changed by that invasion. And then there are the areas where there is still an active invasion." "We talked about the Dread Commanders as being the lieutenants in Diablo's army, and they are kind of roaming the world and controlling different parts of Sanctuary. When a Dread Commander is in an area in Sanctuary, it is an active invasion zone. It will feel like the forest fire is raging now. That represents the future of Sanctuary, should the player not succeed in kicking Diablo out. As you know, that's what Sanctuary will be forever. And so that's how we think about the world, as kind of three different layers of visual storytelling." But there is still some hope during these dark times, as senior production director Tiffany Wat outlined how the game's story about a march to reclaim a lost legacy will eventually push players to become the saviours of humanity. "Humanity is worth fighting for, and as the heir to Westmarch, not only are you fighting for humanity, but you're trying to claim back the kingdom that is yours," Wat said. "And that is where it's a little bit different from the past, where, as the Wanderer, you may not have as much of a personal stake in trying to defeat Diablo. But now, as the heir of Westmarch, this is your land; somebody else has conquered it, and that person happens to be Diablo. And so, as you're trying to survive and you're on the run, in the campaign, you're going to be meeting some survivors and forming that caravan, and it's going to start very small." "As you progress through the story and you find the opportunity to meet other survivors of the apocalypse, and hopefully they're trustworthy enough to join you in your caravan. There's a lot of great visual storytelling there as you're progressing through the game, fighting back the darkness, and your campfire is growing because your caravan is growing, right? So if a jeweler joins you, they're going to bring their wagon. If a blacksmith joins you, then the wagon circle will grow. And I love Oregon Trail, so I think this is a really cool metaphor. I think as you're traveling through the dark world, just the idea that you are making progress and that you're going to hopefully have an opportunity to become victorious in the end, I mean, that's what you're fighting for." Blizzard has big plans for Diablo 5 ahead of its 2029 launch, as it seeks to bring the best of previous games in the series to this new adventure. Fans of the loot grind can look forward to chasing down set items, and with so many classes to choose from, expect plenty of reasons to start a fresh run in Sanctuary.

WoW Devs Confirm Paladins Are A “Dad Class”
description: World of Warcraft has plenty of classes for players to choose from, but according to the game's senior game designer, Josh Greenfield, there's one class that has earned a very specific reputation. Speaking to GameSpot at BlizzCon, Greenfield and senior art director Jeff Parrott discussed their favorite and most-played classes. While Parrott confirmed that his is Hunter, Greenfield's infamous inclination toward the Paladin was discussed a little more in depth. He said that the Paladin is "certainly" a dad class, adding, "You know, I'm not a dad, I'm a dog dad, but I've got the dad bod, so Paladin is totally a dad class." So, straight from a World of Warcraft developer: Paladin is officially a dad class. His choice certainly fits the stereotype, since Paladins are heavily armored, can heal their allies, protect their party, and generally have the sort of dependable, responsible toolkit you'd expect from the class entrusted with keeping everyone else alive while still dealing impressive damage. Of course, being a Paladin isn't actually restricted to dads, but if you've ever encountered a Paladin player who seems particularly enthusiastic about keeping the party organized, now you know why. It's only a matter of time before Paladins start asking to take care of everyone's passport in the departure lounge. The WoW Forever Beta Starts This Week, Here’s How To Get Access
description: At this year's BlizzCon, Blizzard announced a new version of World of Warcraft Classic, called World of Warcraft Forever. Blizzard says WoW Forever is "built as a new permanent home alongside modern and Classic WoW." It's set after the events of Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom but before Molten Core, and sends players back to the original continents with a cap at level 60. There are new stories, a new class, and over 1,000 new quests in the title. With World of Warcraft Forever launching on November 4, a beta is due to start this week. There are a few ways you can gain access, so here's all you need to know. https://youtu.be/uQuKE0KDgiM WoW Forever beta start and end times The World of Warcraft Forever beta will run from Thursday, September 17, to October 21, 2026. There are no official start times just yet, although Blizzard often rolls its updates out between 11 AM and 2 PM ET, so we'd expect the beta to become available around then. How to access the WoW Forever beta There are a few ways you can gain access to the WoW Forever beta, although preordering and buying specific packs are the only guaranteed ways. Beta access is including with the Skyborne Epic Pack and Warcraft Forever Collection. The Skyborne Epic Pack is priced at $59.99 / £51.99, and the Warcraft Forever Collection is priced at $79.99 / £69.99, and both can be bought from the Battle.net store. You can also head to the WoW Forever website and opt-in to the beta, although this is not a guaranteed method of entry. The only way to guarantee entry is by preordering one of the above packs. However, you don't need to buy these packs to get entry to WoW Forever when it releases. That's included with your World of Warcraft subscription or game time. However, if you want access to the new Skyborne race, you'll have to upgrade. WoW Forever early name reservation You'll be able to reserve your WoW Forever name from October 27 through November 3, 2026, and that's included with any upgrade purchase. You can create and customize up to three characters during this period, and character names are reserved on a first-come, first-served basis. WoW Forever beta level cap While WoW Forever will be capped at level 60, the beta will initially be capped at level 20, increasing to level 30 after a few weeks. There's a host of new content coming with WoW Forever, including the Skyborne race, new dungeons, new raids, and an additional PvP battleground. It'll be released on November 4.

title: Diablo 5 Is Bringing Back Set Items, But Wants To Avoid Their Biggest Problem
description: One of the most satisfying things about the Diablo games is their loot grind, and in Diablo 5, Blizzard has plans to keep you clicking enemies to death for a long time in pursuit of an elusive piece of armor or weapon. While it's still early days in terms of how itemization will be handled in the game, Blizzard has confirmed that gear-based sets will return. Set items were originally absent from Diablo 4 when the game launched in 2023, although set bonuses were later added through the Talisman system. Instead of armor collections, players could equip passive bonuses, set effects, and unique powers without needing to replace their current gear. "Something we talk about a lot on the team is we want Diablo 5 to be a game that feels like it has elements for you, regardless of which Diablo game was your favorite," executive producer Matt Zitterman said to GameSpot at BlizzCon. "Clearly, there's some inspiration being taken from Diablo 2 there, but we're also looking at Diablo 4 and the successes we've had there, and are pulling forward ideas from there as well as Diablo 3. "I think for us, Diablo 5 represents this really special moment in the franchise's history where we get to look at the past and bring forward things that feel really familiar, but give them a fresh take." https://youtu.be/Y8HaSFXR7tU "We want to bring set items back. The set system in Diablo 4 worked really well for that game, but something about the way that set items worked in Diablo 2 and Diablo 3, they create kind of like a little quest, right? You want to go like you're on a long-term journey to collect the pieces of this set to unlock something really important about the build you're chasing. We want to bring that forward into Diablo 5. We want to create moments where players feel motivated, not just by a quest log, but by the loot chase. And I think set items, done right, do a really great job of that. We have ideas about how we can overcome some of the challenges of set items, narrowing the itemization game more than broadening it." For more on Diablo 5--which won't be out until 2029--you can read up on how Blizzard wants to make combat feel more visceral than ever before, why the studio went for a new numbered game instead of another Diablo 4 expansion, and how you'll have a broader selection of classes to choose from when you return to Sanctuary.

title: The Best Overwatch Heroes, According To Blizzard
description: If you've ever wondered which Overwatch heroes the people actually making the game enjoy playing, the answer is surprisingly varied. At BlizzCon 2026, GameSpot spoke with Overwatch game director Aaron Keller and associate game director Alec Dawson about their personal favorites, their original mains, and the newer heroes they think you should be playing. Here are the best Overwatch heroes according to Blizzard developers: Lucio For Dawson, it all started with Lucio. "My first main, like, 'I want to play this character all the time,' was Lucio, he said. That's mostly down to Lucio's impressive movement, he explained. "When there's a character with very fluid mobility, I'm like, 'I'm going to lock in and learn as much as I can about this hero.'" Lucio's mobility is one of the defining things about his kit. He can wall ride, allowing him to move quickly around the map by chaining movement across walls rather than taking the ground approach. His Crossfade also gives him an area-of-effect speed boost which applies to any teammates within the radius. Combined with wall riding, this makes him especially good at quickly repositioning, escaping danger, chasing enemies, or returning to the point after death, as Dawson agrees. "I think Lucio just spoke to me on a level--I was like, 'Wait, I can do all of those things?' This guy's slide-sliding around walls! That was awesome from the start." And yes, you can count on it that Dawson has used Lucio's Soundwave to boop more than a few opponents down the well in Ilios. Tracer For Aaron Keller, his original main was Tracer. As someone who has been working on Overwatch from its inception, Keller's endorsement of the hero from the original roster is glowing. "I don't know if I have a main now, but my first was probably Tracer," he explained. "I just loved the mechanics. I feel like the kit is almost perfect, the way that it works." Tracer's kit is built around speed, mobility, and constant repositioning, which helps to explain why Keller finds it "almost perfect." Using her Blink ability, she can teleport a short distance, and it has multiple charges to escape danger quickly. She can then hit her Recall ability to essentially rewind to where she was a few moments earlier, restoring her previous health and ammo. Then there are her Pulse Pistols, which do huge damage at close range. It's that coherence and synchronicity that Keller loves. While he ends up taking the tank role pretty often these days, when he's playing damage, he'll opt for Tracer, although he admits, "I'm a lot worse at damage than I used to be." Reinhardt, Winston, Zayra, and Orisa When he is playing tank, Keller has several favorites rather than one definitive main. "I typically queue flex now, which means I typically queue tank now, is what happens. So, I rotate through a few of the tanks, between Reinhardt, Winston, I love playing Zarya. I'll play Orisa, also," he explained. If you're wondering which tanks have the seal of approval from one of Overwatch's key developers, that's Keller's shortlist. Doctrine When it comes to the newer heroes, Dawson singled out Doctrine as an example of the development team getting many different elements right at once. "Doctrine is a wonderful example of taking an art visual archetype that we hadn't explored yet, this techno-vampire, making it the Overwatch version of that, with all the gameplay bundled together for his drones," he said. "I thought that was just a really perfect sandwich of things all coming together." He's not alone in his admiration for Doctrine, though, as Keller agreed with him. "It's like this amazing combination of backstory, visuals, and gameplay that really supports this, sort of, vampire fantasy," he added. Doctrine takes the classic vampire concept and mixes it with Overwatch's futuristic sci-fi world. Instead of making a traditionally supernatural vampire, Blizzard created the "techno-vampire" by combining classic vampire imagery with futuristic technology. Doctrine has the seal of approval from both developers. That's probably as close as you can get to an official developer-certified hero recommendation. Shion Dawson's personal favorite among the newer heroes is Shion. "I think the one that I personally vibe with the most, 'cause it was just over the top, is Shion," he noted. And the developers apparently knew exactly what kind of hero they wanted Shion to be from the beginning. "From the very get-go we were basing this off some action movies; we need to kick a motorcycle from the air. It was like we're going crazy with this hero," Dawson explained. It seems Shion's personality is something that the developers feel connects her to players. "She just had that personality that's, sort of, villainous to her that I think also struck a really nice chord with people." It's those over-the-top, action-movie-inspired, slightly villainous elements that Dawson thinks resonate particularly well with players. Her personality matches the extravagance of her concept, and she's certainly not designed to be understated. Emre Keller's pick of the newer heroes is a little less flashy, but that's exactly where his praise is aimed. "I think the primary file of Emre feels so good," he explained. That primary fire is Emre's Synthetic Burst Rifle, a three-round burst weapon. That straightforward, satisfying burst-rifle shooting makes Emre easy to learn how to play. "Overwatch is a first-person shooter, so you just want a weapon like that in the game," Keller explained. "He might not be the flashiest character that we've got, but he has really resonated with a lot of players, and I think one of the reasons is that primary fire." While these heroes come highly recommended, they didn't always function in the way that you see today. Tracer used to shoot lasers from her eyes, while two of Overwatch's most-criticized characters are getting a rework.

title: Blizzard Says Diablo 5 Was Too Big To Be A Diablo 4 Expansion
description: Diablo 4 is far from dead, but don't expect any new expansions for the game going forward. Instead, Blizzard is preparing to tell the darkest story yet in Diablo 5, one that required a new numbered game to properly reintroduce Diablo himself back to the series, following his defeat in 2012's Diablo 3. Currently aiming for a 2029 release, this would mean that players are in for a relatively short wait for a new Diablo game--compared to previous releases--as Diablo 5 will arrive a mere six years after Diablo 4. Speaking to GameSpot at BlizzCon, Diablo senior production director Tiffany Wat and executive producer Matt Zitterman explained that it made sense for Blizzard to move to a new Diablo so that the studio could make structural changes to the game--changes that would have been very challenging to pull off within the framework of a Diablo 4 expansion. "It really started by looking at who our players are," Zitterman said. "Who are Diablo players? Why are they playing Diablo? What do they want out of a Diablo game? That is a really critical step in the early conceptual phase for a game, even before you're thinking about, like, 'Gosh, should we make this an expansion? Should we make it a sequel? How do we do this?' Looking at past examples, looking at what's working well in Diablo 4, where there are opportunities for improvement, and we kind of build our ambition for the game at the conceptual phase through those avenues of information." https://youtu.be/Y8HaSFXR7tU "And as we started to understand and kind of solidify what that ambition was, it became very clear to us pretty early that in order to achieve what we wanted to achieve with this game, we needed to make some more deeply structural changes to the way the game works, changes that are just frankly hard to do in an expansion. Again, it's all about figuring out what the best way is to make the best Diablo game we can for players. Diablo is the main villain. Diablo is the guy that we want to tell a real story about. We want to tell a story that's on par with--and hopefully exceeds--the story we told with Lilith and Mephisto." "And to do that in an expansion just didn't feel right. We needed to give him his own game." Player feedback also plays a vital role in the development of Diablo 5, and Zitterman said that by announcing the game this early, Blizzard could make important changes well ahead of the game's eventual launch. "If we didn't announce now and we kind of held back until we were much further along in development, at that point, it's much harder to take that feedback and use it to make those really important changes and refinements to the game throughout development," Zitterman explained. For more on Diablo 5, you can learn how combat could be even more ferocious, how the game will offer more character classes than ever, and how the Plague Knight uses the grossest powers to stay a step ahead of Diablo's demonic armies.

title: Wardogs Devs Are Watching Economy Cheaters Like Hawks
description: With the FPS Wardogs dominating the Steam charts, developer Bulkhead is paying close attention to the game's various systems. The studio recently dropped a new patch that makes some necessary changes for server stability, while confirming that the team has their eyes on cheaters and exploiters. As part of Patch 0.11, which came out on September 14, Bulkhead announced that should any dogs of war take advantage of Wardogs' economy by farming servers, they'll find themselves either temporarily or permanently banned from the game. "As an early access game, we’re not perfect, and we never will be," Bulkhead said in the patch notes. "But if you do find something and take advantage of it, we have decided to come down hard." To be specific, Bulkhead outlined three different scenarios that will come with three different repercussions depending on the type of exploit you partake in. Scenario 1: Stockpiling money by abusing cash exploits and bugs will result in a timed ban, with the length determined by whether you were banned previously. Your cash and experience will get reset, too. Scenario 2: Showing economy exploits through tutorial content will be treated as "advertising cheats," resulting in a permanent ban. However, if you happen to stumble upon an exploit and share that with Bulkhead on Discord or social media, that'll be seen as an "alert," which prevents you from being permanently banned. Scenario 3: If you're farming experience via server exploits, which Bulkhead says will result in "the most serious bans," your account will get banned permanently. The studio clarified, though, that it's open to feedback on this policy, stating that these positions could change if enough people believe they're too harsh. "In the very early stages of finding these issues you may find yourself getting away with it, but it doesn't take long for our backend data to flag abusers," Bulkhead said, "Effectively, if you find something and you then keep doing it, over and over again, that is abuse of an exploit. If you figure something out and test it once or twice, no biggy, thanks for helping us QA." Wardogs is currently Steam's hottest game right now, with over 320,000 people playing at the time of writing. It didn't have the smoothest of starts, but the kinks are getting ironed out as the days go on. Players are a little riled up at the moment, though, particularly because people don't know how to close the door behind them.

title: How WoW Forever Handles Its Massive Set Of New Quests
description: One of the big announcements at BlizzCon was WoW Forever, the next iteration of offering a classic-style WoW experience. Blizzard is hoping to draw players back to the OG WoW in a number of ways, including with the introduction of 1,000+ new quests. GameSpot caught up with Blizzard senior game designer Josh Greenfield to discuss this, along with why the game's OG quests--from 22 years ago--still resonate today. If Blizzard is adding 1,000 more quests to WoW with the update, how many does that bring the game up to in total? It's a tricky question to answer, Greenfield said, in part because some of WoW's original quests are "tracking quests," but if you're counting "actual playable quests," the game has around 3,000 to 3,500. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IEMrosrAVH0 So with 1,000+ more added of actual playable quests, that's a significant increase. WoW Forever also adds four new zones, and each of these has between 50 and 200 quests, so that's where many will come from. Additionally, the existing zones have been "glowed up," with the Wetlands and Azshara, specifically, getting a "lot of new quests to round them out as zones." "Every nook and cranny, you're going to find something, even from like level five ... onward, you're going to start seeing new stuff," Greenfield said. Also in our interview, we asked how Blizzard came up with the inspirations for the 1,000 new quests, and if there might be a new version of The Green Hills of Stranglethorn, which is regarded as perhaps the game's worst quest. Greenfield said that was "kind of a terrible quest," but it still has charm and remains memorable even to this day. A lot of the original WoW is full of similarly memorable and "super iconic" quests, Greenfield said, and Blizzard is keen to carry the torch forward with WoW Forever. "I think a lot of those quests explored the world at a very like ground level, and they they told stories at a very like ground level, a very like relatable level. You know, 'I am not the hero, I am a hero, and I'm going on this adventure with my dented shield and rusty sword.' And, you know, like things like The Missing Diplomat and things like that, like being able to kind of jet-set around the world and talk to different people and learn more about the cultures of each of these different zones, and learn a mystery and try and unravel a mystery." Greenfield teased that Blizzard might "help finish unraveling that mystery" in WoW Forever. He went on to say some of the original WoW's quests were dark and grim, and Blizzard is embracing that philosophy with a lot of the new quests. "Even Zephyr Isle, it's in the sky, it's nice and bright, but it's the story once you get into it, it's not it's not all, you know, sunshine and rainbows up there. It can be a little little hard," he said. WoW Forever releases on November 4. In addition to the new zones and quests, players can expected update class designs, revamped systems, visual and gameplay improvements, and an expanded list of race and class options. Players can access WoW Forever via their existing WoW subscription. However, players can buy the $80 Warcraft Forever Collection to receive the new Skyborne race, beta access, and early name reservation for WoW Forever. The Collection also includes Warcraft III: Reforged and Warcraft III: Reforged Forsaken Kingdom
